VBO:0200038.summary: Merry and people-oriented, the American Cocker Spaniel often brings an outgoing warmth to companionship while retaining a keen interest in work. Its sporting roots lie in flushing game from cover; the American breed developed from imported English Cockers and became a separate breed in the mid-twentieth century.
VBO:0200038.shortDescription: An outgoing, people-oriented spaniel, the American Cocker often keeps its merry character and willingness to work.

sources.title: United Kennel Club: Cocker Spaniel breed standard
sources.evidence: The History section explicitly distinguishes American from English Cockers, describes early English imports and flushing game, and records separate recognition in1947. Characteristics describes people-oriented, merry temperament and inclination to work; head, ears, body, coat and feet sections define compact sturdy sporting anatomy.

sources.title: Canadian Kennel Club: American Cocker Spaniel
sources.evidence: Temperament describes an outgoing friendly personality; Activity Level notes inclination to work and present companion role. Origin explains development from imported Cockers in North America and eventual separation from English Cocker. Breed-page photograph credited to Nadia Bongelli shows an adult-appearing black American Cocker, rounded but moderate crown, pronounced stop, deep short muzzle with full lips, low-set long silky hanging ears; seated pose does not establish unseen hind feet/tail.

sources.title: Royal Kennel Club: Spaniel (American Cocker) breed standard
sources.evidence: Characteristics describes willingness to work and merry character. Undocked tail section states moderate length, thicker root tapering to tip, proportionate feathering, carried at topline or a little above and never curled over back. Coat section limits feathering so body lines and sporting function remain visible.
